newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello yesterday announced changes to the way in which depreciation is to be calculated on assets of tax-exempt entities that enter the tax base when privatised. This change in tax policy could slash billions of dollars from the revenues of future privatisations by the State Governments. Page 1.

Foster's Brewing Group Ltd is set to acquire the world's second largest wine mail-order group, Cellarmaster Wines, for A$160 million. Cellarmaster had been considering a float on the stock exchange but was flooded with offers by Foster's, Coles and other wine groups over the last few months. Page 1.

The survey of monthly job advertisements, released yesterday by the ANZ Banking Group, has revealed that employment growth fell by 2.9 per cent in seasonally adjusted terms in July. The figures show that job creation is occurring at only half the rate foecast by the Federal Government. A special Cabinet meeting on unemployment will today examine ways to reduce the high jobless rate. Page 1.

The Federal Government has asked Indonesia to withdraw an effective import ban on Australian fast ferries following moves by local manufacturers to sell up to six vessels worth A$200 million in Japan during the next year. Federal Transport Minister John harp has made personal representations to senior Indonesian ministers in an attempt to open up the potentially lucrative Indonesian market to domestic ferry manufacturers. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A Cabinet meeting today will be told that any attempt to reduce the current high levels of unemployment will widen the divide between high and low income earners, and that a negative income tax is required to protect those at the bottom of the earnings lader. The release of figures yesterday showing static levels of job growth has highlighted the long-term weakness of the job market. Page 1.

A prayer service was held yesterday at Thredbo village to commemorate the 11 people confirmed dead in the disaster. Rescuers continue searching for the eight people still missing under the ruined ski lodges, their efforts given urgency by the forecast for tomorrow of rain, which could cause further slippage at the site. Page 1.

The growth in overseas visas granted to students from Asian countries has fallen to six per cent in the January to June period, down from the previous figure of 26 per cent. The figures are the first unequivocal evidence that the Pauline Hanson race controversy is starting to adversely affect Australian business relations with Asia. Page 1.

A woman previously thought to be the pedestrian swept away by last Wednesday's landslide at Thredbo has been found to be safe. Susan Green was initially counted by police as among those trapped within the Bimbadeen and Carrinya lodges, but was soon located with dozens of other Thredbo residents evacuated from the danger zone at the nearby Black Bear Inn. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Federal Government is set to introduce radical changes into its employment strategy as part of its plan to put the Commonwealth Employment Service out to private tender. Released yesterday by Federal Employment Minister Senator Amanda Vanstone, the changes will include defining a "real job" as 15 hours a week work, and finding full-time and permanent jobs for only half of the 800,000 unemployed. Page 1.

A memorial service was held yesterday for the victims of the Thredbo disaster. Governor-General Sir William Deane joined in the prayer service and spoke of how the tragedy of the families who had lost loved ones to the disaster was shared by the wider Autralian community. Page 1.

The Federal Government's higher education review head, Roderick West, has advised against fully deregulating universities, and warned that Australian universities would have difficulty competing with Asian counterparts which received Government financial upport. Speaking at the Isolated Children's Parents Association annual conference, West's comments conflict with the Federal Government's aim of allowing universities to offer undergraduate places to students who pay full tuition fees. Page 1.

Health insurance funds and private hospitals have agreed to Federal Government proposals that will see patients in the private system who wish to claim for rehabiliation in hospital face increased scrutiny and restrictions to services. The move is in exchange for an agreement by the health funds and private hospitals to maintain rehabilitation and palliative care in all private health insurance policies. Page 2.
THE AGE

Concerns have been raised for the safety of rescue workers at the Thredbo disaster site. Engineers attempted yesterday to secure the Schuss Lodge, whose foundations were undermined by last Wednesday's landslide which caused two lodges to collapse and killed 19 people. Page 1.

The Federal Government last night announced it was clamping down on the tax deductions that can be claimed by buyers of privatised State businesses. The move is expected to slash A$300 million off Victoria's gas and electricity asset sales next year, and has been condemned by Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale as a "blatant rip-off". Page 1.

The Howard Florey Institute in Melbourne, in conjunction with Rockefeller University in New York, has conducted exciting new research which could enable people to shed up to 15 per cent of their body weight without changing their eating habits. The findings are to be published today in the US science journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Science, which relates how the hormone leptin can be used to decrease appetite. Page 1.

The SA Government is under siege from a serial leaker, who appears to have unrestricted access to State Government papers. The damaging leaks have, to date, forced the resignation of former Premier Dean Brown and Cabinet Minister Dale Baker, and are believed to have influenced Premier John Olsen to postpone the upcoming State election to the new year. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
